correctness.rationale: The domain inequalities force strict alternation and give the exact increasing quartic left-side return. Its monotonicity proves global convergence and excludes all periods other than two. Solving \(H=H\prime=0\) yields \(qu(4-3u)=1\), the two explicit K folds and the triple cusp; endpoint signs prevent uncounted roots. Exact factorization at \(q=k=4/5\) gives three interior roots, their multipliers, and a right-side basin threshold; cusp local expansion proves the universal 2/3 square-root convergence constant. All symbolic identities and seven rational root-count cases were checked by running the embedded checker.
